name: Neolithic settlement at Mehrgarh
summary: Early farming settlement in Baluchistan with evidence of cultivated barley and wheat and domesticated animals.
note: Earliest levels dated c. 7000-6000 BCE depending on source.

name: Excavation of Harappa begins
summary: Excavations at Harappa bring the Harappan (Indus) civilisation to light.

name: Excavation of Mohenjo-daro begins
summary: R.D. Banerji begins work at Mohenjo-daro.

name: Mature Harappan phase
summary: Urban phase with planned cities, standardised weights and the Indus script.
note: Textbook ranges vary (e.g. c. 2600-1900 or 2500-1750 BCE).

name: Decline of Harappan urbanism
summary: De-urbanisation of the major Harappan sites; causes are debated.

name: Early (Rig) Vedic period
summary: Period of composition of most of the Rig Veda; largely pastoral society in the Sapta Sindhu region.
note: Chronology is debated.

name: Later Vedic period
summary: Expansion into the Ganga plains, use of iron, settled agriculture and sharper varna divisions.

name: Age of the sixteen Mahajanapadas
summary: Territorial states such as Magadha, Kosala, Vatsa and Avanti emerge in north India.

name: Achaemenid control of Gandhara
summary: Gandhara and the Indus region appear as provinces of the Persian Achaemenid empire.

name: Life of Gautama Buddha (traditional dates)
summary: Founder of Buddhism.
note: Many historians now place his death c. 400 BCE (short chronology).

name: Life of Vardhamana Mahavira
summary: Twenty-fourth Jain tirthankara.
note: Jain tradition gives 599-527 BCE.

name: Reign of Bimbisara of Magadha
summary: Haryanka ruler who expanded Magadha by conquest (Anga) and marriage alliances.
note: Traditional dates tied to the Buddha's chronology.

name: First Buddhist Council at Rajagriha
summary: Held soon after the Buddha's death to compile his teachings.
note: Date depends on the Buddha's death date.

name: Alexander's campaign in north-west India
summary: Macedonian campaign in the north-west; the army refused to go beyond the Beas.

name: Battle of the Hydaspes (Jhelum)
aliases: Hydaspes|Battle of the Jhelum|Alexander and Porus
summary: Alexander defeats Porus and reinstates him as ruler.

name: Chandragupta Maurya founds the Mauryan empire
aliases: Chandragupta Maurya|foundation of the Mauryan empire
summary: Chandragupta overthrows the Nandas.
note: Dates range c. 324-321 BCE.

name: War and treaty with Seleucus Nicator
summary: Seleucus cedes north-western territories; Megasthenes later comes as envoy to Pataliputra.

name: Accession of Ashoka
summary: Ashoka succeeds Bindusara.
note: Accession dated c. 273-268 BCE in different works.

name: Kalinga War
summary: Conquest of Kalinga; Rock Edict XIII records Ashoka's remorse and turn to dhamma.
note: Eighth year after Ashoka's consecration.

name: Third Buddhist Council at Pataliputra
summary: Held under Ashoka; followed by missions to spread Buddhism.
note: Known mainly from Sri Lankan chronicles.

name: End of the Mauryan dynasty
summary: Pushyamitra Shunga kills the last Maurya ruler and founds the Shunga dynasty.

name: James Prinsep deciphers Brahmi
summary: Decipherment that made Ashoka's edicts readable.

name: Indo-Greek king Menander (Milinda)
summary: Best-known Indo-Greek ruler; his dialogue with Nagasena is the Milindapanha.

name: Start of the Vikrama Samvat era
summary: Era reckoned from 57 BCE, traditionally linked to a king Vikramaditya of Ujjain.
note: The era's origin is debated; its starting year is fixed.

name: Start of the Shaka era
summary: Era beginning in 78 CE; later adopted for India's national calendar.
note: Traditionally linked to Kanishka; the link is contested.

name: Accession of Kanishka
summary: Leading Kushana ruler; patron of Buddhism and of the Gandhara and Mathura schools of art.
note: Older view 78 CE (Shaka era); many scholars now prefer c. 127 CE.

name: Reign of Gautamiputra Satakarni
summary: Satavahana ruler who defeated the Kshaharata Shaka Nahapana (Nasik inscription).
note: Chronologies vary.

name: Junagadh (Girnar) inscription of Rudradaman
summary: Early long Sanskrit inscription; records repair of the Sudarshana lake.
note: Dated Shaka year 72.

name: Sangam age
summary: Age of early Tamil poetry and the Chera, Chola and Pandya chiefdoms.
note: Ranges differ widely between scholars.

name: Start of the Gupta era
summary: Gupta era begins in 319-320 CE, usually linked to Chandragupta I's accession.

name: Reign of Samudragupta
summary: Gupta expansion recorded in Harishena's Prayag (Allahabad) prashasti.

name: Reign of Chandragupta II
summary: Defeat of the Western Kshatrapas; height of Gupta power.

name: Faxian (Fa-Hien) travels to India
summary: Chinese Buddhist pilgrim whose account describes north India under Chandragupta II.
note: 399-414 spans the whole journey from and back to China.

name: Reign of Kumaragupta I
summary: Gupta ruler traditionally credited with founding the Nalanda mahavihara.

name: Reign of Skandagupta
summary: Repulsed early Huna attacks.

name: Aryabhata composes the Aryabhatiya
summary: Astronomical and mathematical treatise.

name: Defeat of the Huna ruler Mihirakula
summary: Yashodharman of Malwa claims victory over Mihirakula (Mandsaur inscription).

name: Reign of Harshavardhana
summary: Ruler of Thanesar and Kannauj, known from the Harshacharita and Xuanzang's account.

name: Xuanzang (Hiuen Tsang) in India
summary: Chinese pilgrim who studied at Nalanda and attended Harsha's assemblies.

name: Pulakeshin II stops Harsha on the Narmada
summary: Chalukya victory over Harsha, recorded in the Aihole inscription.
note: Dated c. 618-619 or c. 630-634 CE in different works.

name: Aihole inscription of Pulakeshin II
summary: Prashasti by Ravikirti recording Pulakeshin II's victories.
note: Dated Shaka 556.

name: Pallava capture of Vatapi
summary: Pallava king Narasimhavarman I sacks the Chalukya capital; Pulakeshin II dies.

name: Arab conquest of Sindh
aliases: Muhammad bin Qasim|Arab conquest of Sindh
summary: Umayyad general Muhammad bin Qasim defeats Dahir and conquers Sindh.
note: Campaign of 711-712.

name: Tripartite struggle for Kannauj
summary: Long contest between Palas, Gurjara-Pratiharas and Rashtrakutas for control of Kannauj.

name: Reign of Dharmapala
summary: Pala ruler of Bengal; founder of the Vikramashila mahavihara.

name: Kailasa temple at Ellora
summary: Rock-cut temple excavated under the Rashtrakuta king Krishna I.

name: Reign of Amoghavarsha I
summary: Long-reigning Rashtrakuta king; the Kannada work Kavirajamarga is associated with his court.

name: Reign of Mihira Bhoja
summary: Most powerful Gurjara-Pratihara ruler.

name: Reign of Rajaraja I
summary: Chola expansion; built the Brihadishvara temple at Thanjavur (completed c. 1010).

name: Reign of Rajendra I
summary: Expeditions to the Ganga valley and Srivijaya; new capital at Gangaikonda Cholapuram.

name: Raids of Mahmud of Ghazni
summary: Series of about seventeen raids into north India.

name: Mahmud's raid on Somnath
summary: Sack of the Somnath temple in Gujarat.

name: Alberuni's Kitab-ul-Hind
summary: Account of Indian society, science and religion.

name: First Battle of Tarain
summary: Prithviraj Chauhan defeats Muhammad of Ghur.

name: Second Battle of Tarain
summary: Muhammad of Ghur defeats Prithviraj; opens north India to Ghurid rule.

name: Battle of Chandawar
summary: Muhammad of Ghur defeats Jaichand of Kannauj.

name: Bakhtiyar Khalji's raid on Nadia
summary: Raid on the Sena capital that began Turkish rule in Bengal.
note: Dated c. 1202-1205 in different accounts.

name: Qutbuddin Aibak rules at Delhi
aliases: Qutbuddin Aibak|Delhi Sultanate founded|Mamluk dynasty|Slave dynasty
summary: After Muhammad of Ghur's death Aibak rules as the first sultan of Delhi.

name: Reign of Iltutmish
summary: Consolidated the Sultanate; received investiture from the Abbasid caliph.

name: Reign of Raziya
summary: Only woman ruler of the Delhi Sultanate.

name: Reign of Balban
summary: Stressed royal prestige and broke the power of the Turkish nobility (the Forty).

name: Khalji revolution
summary: The Khaljis replace the Ilbari Turks on the Delhi throne.

name: Reign of Alauddin Khalji
summary: Market control, revenue measures and campaigns in Gujarat, Rajasthan and the Deccan.

name: Alauddin captures Chittor
summary: Siege and capture of Chittor.

name: Malik Kafur's southern campaigns
summary: Campaigns against Warangal, Dwarasamudra and Madurai.

name: Reign of Muhammad bin Tughlaq
summary: Reign known for ambitious and controversial projects.

name: Capital moved to Daulatabad
summary: Shift of the capital, and many inhabitants, from Delhi to Daulatabad.

name: Token currency experiment
summary: Bronze tokens issued at par with silver; withdrawn after widespread forgery.

name: Ibn Battuta in India
summary: Moroccan traveller who served as qazi of Delhi; described India in his Rihla.

name: Foundation of Vijayanagara
summary: Founded by Harihara and Bukka of the Sangama dynasty.
note: 1336 is the traditional date.

name: Foundation of the Bahmani kingdom
summary: Revolt against Muhammad bin Tughlaq creates an independent Deccan sultanate.

name: Reign of Firoz Shah Tughlaq
summary: Canals, new towns, and jizya extended to Brahmins.

name: Timur sacks Delhi
summary: Timur's invasion and sack of Delhi.

name: Lodi dynasty
summary: Afghan dynasty ended by Babur at Panipat.

name: Reign of Krishnadevaraya
summary: Peak of Vijayanagara power; author of the Telugu Amuktamalyada.

name: Battle of Raichur
summary: Krishnadevaraya defeats the sultan of Bijapur.

name: First Battle of Panipat
summary: Babur defeats Ibrahim Lodi and founds Mughal rule.

name: Battle of Khanwa
summary: Babur defeats Rana Sanga's Rajput confederacy.
note: Day given as 16 or 17 March.

name: Sher Shah defeats Humayun (Chausa and Kannauj)
summary: Chausa (1539) and Kannauj (1540) drive Humayun out of India.

name: Reign of Sher Shah Suri
summary: Administrative and revenue reforms, the silver rupiya, road building.

name: Accession of Akbar
summary: Akbar is enthroned at Kalanaur after Humayun's death.

name: Second Battle of Panipat
summary: Mughal victory over Hemu.

name: Battle of Talikota (Rakshasa-Tangadi)
summary: Combined Deccan sultanates defeat Vijayanagara; the capital is sacked.
note: Day given as 23 or 26 January.

name: Mansabdari system organised
summary: Graded ranks for nobles and officials.
note: The dual zat/sawar rank is dated to the 1590s.

name: Ibadat Khana built at Fatehpur Sikri
summary: Hall for religious debate.

name: Battle of Haldighati
summary: Mughal forces under Man Singh fight Maharana Pratap.
note: Day given as 18 or 21 June.

name: Mahzar declaration
summary: Gives Akbar the final word on disputed religious questions.

name: Dahsala (zabt) revenue system
summary: Revenue assessed on ten-year averages of produce and prices.

name: Din-i-Ilahi (Tauhid-i-Ilahi)
summary: Discipleship order centred on the emperor.

name: Execution of Guru Arjan
summary: Fifth Sikh Guru, compiler of the Adi Granth, executed on Jahangir's orders.

name: Sir Thomas Roe at Jahangir's court
summary: English ambassador seeking trading privileges.

name: Battle of Samugarh
summary: Aurangzeb defeats Dara Shikoh in the war of succession.

name: Treaty of Purandar
summary: Shivaji cedes forts to the Mughals.

name: Battle of Saraighat
summary: Ahom victory over the Mughals on the Brahmaputra.

name: Coronation of Shivaji
summary: Shivaji crowned Chhatrapati at Raigad.

name: Execution of Guru Tegh Bahadur
summary: Ninth Sikh Guru executed at Delhi.

name: Founding of the Khalsa
summary: Founded at Anandpur.

name: Death of Aurangzeb
summary: Followed by succession wars and weakening central control.

name: Farrukhsiyar's farman to the English Company
summary: Grants the English Company duty-free trade in Bengal.

name: Baji Rao I as Peshwa
summary: Northward expansion of Maratha power.

name: Nizam-ul-Mulk wins at Shakar Kheda
summary: Leads to the autonomous state of Hyderabad.

name: Nadir Shah's invasion
summary: Mughal defeat at Karnal and sack of Delhi; the Peacock Throne is carried away.

name: Third Battle of Panipat
summary: Afghan victory over the Marathas.

name: Amir Khusrau
summary: Poet and musician at the Sultanate court; disciple of Nizamuddin Auliya.

name: Death of Nizamuddin Auliya
summary: Chishti Sufi of Delhi.

name: Kabir
summary: Nirguna bhakti poet of Banaras.
note: Traditional and uncertain dates.

name: Life of Guru Nanak
summary: Founder of Sikhism.

name: Chaitanya Mahaprabhu
summary: Leader of Gaudiya Vaishnavism in Bengal.

name: Vasco da Gama reaches Calicut
summary: Opens the sea route from Europe to India round the Cape.

name: Portuguese capture Goa
summary: Goa becomes the centre of the Portuguese Estado da India.

name: English East India Company chartered
summary: Royal charter to the London company trading to the East Indies.

name: English factory at Surat
summary: First permanent English factory in Mughal India.

name: Carnatic Wars
summary: Three Anglo-French wars in south India (1746-48, 1749-54, 1756-63).

name: Battle of Wandiwash
summary: Decisive British victory over the French.

name: Treaty of Allahabad and grant of the Diwani
summary: Company obtains the diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa.

name: Dual government in Bengal
summary: Company held the diwani while the nizamat stayed nominally with the Nawab.

name: Regulating Act
summary: Governor of Bengal made Governor-General; Supreme Court at Calcutta.

name: Pitt's India Act
summary: Board of Control set up over the Company.

name: Treaty of Salbai
summary: Ends the First Anglo-Maratha War.

name: Permanent Settlement
summary: Land revenue fixed in perpetuity with zamindars in Bengal.

name: Subsidiary alliance system
summary: Hyderabad is the first to accept (1798).

name: Fall of Seringapatam; death of Tipu Sultan
Treaty of Bassein
summary: Peshwa accepts a subsidiary alliance; leads to the Second Anglo-Maratha War.

name: Anglo-Maratha Wars
summary: Three wars (1775-82, 1803-05, 1817-18); the Peshwaship is abolished in 1818.

name: Treaty of Amritsar
summary: Sutlej fixed as the eastern limit of Ranjit Singh's kingdom.

name: Charter Act of 1813
summary: Ends the Company's India trade monopoly (tea and China trade excepted); provides one lakh rupees a year for education.

name: Ryotwari settlement in Madras
summary: Settlement made directly with cultivators.
note: Experiments from 1792; general extension c. 1820.

name: Mahalwari settlement
summary: Village-community (mahal) settlement in the North-Western Provinces.

name: Charter Act of 1833
summary: Governor-General of Bengal becomes Governor-General of India; Company's commercial role ends.

name: Annexation of Punjab
summary: Follows the Second Anglo-Sikh War.

name: Annexations under the Doctrine of Lapse
summary: Satara (1848) first; Jhansi and Nagpur among others.

name: Charter Act of 1853
summary: Introduces open competition for the civil service.

name: Annexation of Awadh
summary: Annexed on grounds of misgovernment.

name: Revolt of 1857 begins at Meerut
aliases: Revolt of 1857|Meerut outbreak|Sepoy Mutiny|First War of Independence

name: Universities of Calcutta, Bombay and Madras founded
Government of India Act 1858
aliases: Government of India Act 1858|Act for the Better Government of India
summary: Rule passes from the Company to the Crown.

name: Indigo revolt
summary: Bengal peasants refuse to grow indigo.

name: Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental school and college at Aligarh
summary: School opened 1875; college 1877.

name: Deccan riots
summary: Peasants attack moneylenders in Poona and Ahmednagar districts.

name: Vernacular Press Act
summary: Repealed in 1882.

name: Indian National Congress founded
aliases: founding of the Indian National Congress|first Congress session
summary: First session held at Bombay.

name: Boycott resolution at Calcutta Town Hall
summary: Formal launch of the Swadeshi movement.

name: Partition of Bengal takes effect
summary: Announced in July 1905.

name: All-India Muslim League founded
summary: Founded at Dacca.

name: Surat split
summary: Congress splits between Moderates and Extremists.

name: Morley-Minto Reforms (Indian Councils Act 1909)
summary: Introduces separate electorates for Muslims.

name: Delhi Durbar announces annulment of the partition
aliases: Delhi Durbar 1911|annulment of the partition of Bengal
summary: Annulment and transfer of the capital to Delhi announced.

name: Ghadar Party founded
summary: Founded in the United States.

name: Home Rule Leagues founded
summary: Tilak's league in April, Besant's in September.

name: Lucknow Pact
summary: Congress-League agreement; Congress accepts separate electorates.

name: Champaran satyagraha
summary: Against the tinkathia system on indigo plantations.

name: Montagu Declaration
summary: Announces the goal of progressive realisation of responsible government.

name: Kheda satyagraha and Ahmedabad mill strike
Rowlatt Act passed
summary: Allows detention without trial.

name: Government of India Act 1919
summary: Introduces dyarchy in the provinces.

name: Non-Cooperation Movement launched
summary: Endorsed at the Calcutta (September) and Nagpur (December) sessions of 1920.

name: Swaraj Party formed
summary: Formed after the Gaya session rejected council entry.
note: Commonly dated 1 January 1923; some works say late 1922-early 1923.

name: Vaikom satyagraha
summary: Agitation for access to roads around the Vaikom temple in Travancore.

name: Simon Commission arrives in India
summary: Appointed November 1927; boycotted because it had no Indian member.

name: Bombs thrown in the Central Legislative Assembly
First Round Table Conference
summary: Congress did not attend.

name: Execution of Bhagat Singh, Rajguru and Sukhdev
Second Round Table Conference
summary: Gandhi attends as the sole Congress representative.

name: Poona Pact
summary: Reserved seats for the depressed classes within joint electorates.

name: Government of India Act 1935
summary: Provincial autonomy and a proposed all-India federation.

name: Congress ministries in office
summary: Resigned in October-November 1939 in protest at India's entry into the war.

name: Lahore Resolution of the Muslim League
summary: Moved on 23 March, adopted on 24 March.

name: Cripps Mission in India
summary: Offers post-war Dominion Status with the right to secede and a right for provinces not to join the new Union; rejected by both Congress and the League.
note: Arrived in Delhi 22 March (some sources say 23 March); left 11 or 12 April.

name: Cripps draft declaration published
note: Handed to the press on 29 March and published on 30 March.

name: Quit India resolution
summary: Passed at Bombay; leaders arrested on 9 August.

name: Provisional Government of Free India (Azad Hind)
aliases: Azad Hind government|Provisional Government of Free India

name: Simla Conference on the Wavell Plan
summary: Broke down over the League's claim to nominate all Muslim members.

name: INA trials at the Red Fort
Royal Indian Navy mutiny
summary: Began in Bombay.

name: Cabinet Mission arrives in India
summary: Three-member British Cabinet delegation.

name: Second Simla Conference (tripartite talks)
summary: Talks between the Mission, Congress and the League end without agreement.

name: Cabinet Mission Plan (statement of 16 May)
aliases: Cabinet Mission Plan|16 May statement|long-term plan
summary: Three-tier union with provinces grouped into Sections A, B and C; Constituent Assembly elected by provincial assemblies; a sovereign Pakistan rejected.

name: Cabinet Mission statement of 25 May
summary: Calls grouping an essential feature of the scheme; says the Congress reading of paragraph 15 does not accord with the Mission's intentions.

name: Muslim League accepts the Plan
aliases: League acceptance of the Cabinet Mission Plan
summary: Accepts, holding that the basis of Pakistan is inherent in compulsory grouping.

name: Interim government proposals (16 June statement)
summary: Viceroy proposes a 14-member interim government.

name: Congress Working Committee resolution on the Plan
aliases: Congress acceptance of the Cabinet Mission Plan
summary: Accepts the 16 May long-term plan with its own reading of grouping; rejects the 16 June interim government proposals.

name: AICC ratifies the Working Committee's decision
Nehru's press conference on the Plan
summary: Says Congress is committed only to entering the Constituent Assembly and that there will probably be no grouping.

name: Muslim League withdraws its acceptance
aliases: League withdrawal from the Cabinet Mission Plan
summary: League Council withdraws acceptance and calls for Direct Action.

name: Direct Action Day and the Great Calcutta Killing
Interim Government headed by Nehru sworn in
Muslim League joins the Interim Government
summary: League nominees join; Liaquat Ali Khan takes Finance.
note: Sources give 25 or 26 October for the swearing-in; the decision to join came in mid-October.

name: British government statement of 6 December
summary: Upholds the Mission's reading that sections decide by majority; offers a Federal Court reference.

name: Constituent Assembly first meets
aliases: first session of the Constituent Assembly
summary: Meets without the Muslim League.

name: Objectives Resolution
summary: Moved on 13 December 1946, adopted on 22 January 1947.

name: Tebhaga movement
summary: Sharecroppers in Bengal demand two-thirds of the crop.

name: Indian Independence Act receives royal assent
Independence of India
summary: Pakistan's independence is dated 14 August.

name: Instrument of Accession of Jammu and Kashmir
Bhoodan movement begins
summary: Begins at Pochampally in Telangana.

name: Andhra State formed
summary: Follows Potti Sriramulu's death on fast in December 1952.

name: Glorious Revolution and Bill of Rights
summary: Parliament settles the Crown on William and Mary; the Bill of Rights limits royal power.

name: Locke's Two Treatises of Government
note: Published late 1689 with 1690 on the title page.

name: Montesquieu's The Spirit of the Laws
summary: Argues for separation of powers.

name: Spinning jenny
note: Invented c. 1764-65; patented 1770.

name: Stamp Act
summary: Colonial protest under the slogan of no taxation without representation.

name: Adam Smith's The Wealth of Nations
British surrender at Saratoga
summary: Leads to the French alliance of 1778.

name: Treaty of Paris (1783)
summary: Britain recognises American independence.

name: US Constitution signed
summary: In force from 1789.

name: Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen
aliases: Declaration of the Rights of Man

name: Reign of Terror
aliases: Reign of Terror|Committee of Public Safety

name: Grito de Dolores (Mexican independence struggle begins)
Battle of Leipzig (Battle of the Nations)
Congress of Vienna
summary: Final Act signed on 9 June 1815.

name: Treaty of Nanking
summary: Hong Kong ceded; treaty ports opened.

name: Revolutions of 1848
summary: Uprisings in France, the German states, the Habsburg lands and Italy.

name: Crimean War
summary: Ended by the Treaty of Paris, 30 March 1856.

name: Emancipation of the serfs in Russia
note: Dated 19 February 1861 in the Old Style calendar.

name: American Civil War begins at Fort Sumter
Triple Alliance
summary: Germany, Austria-Hungary and Italy.

name: First Sino-Japanese War
summary: Ended by the Treaty of Shimonoseki, 17 April 1895.

name: Boxer Rebellion
summary: Ended by the Boxer Protocol, 7 September 1901.

name: Russo-Japanese War
summary: Ended by the Treaty of Portsmouth, 5 September 1905.

name: Bloody Sunday, start of the 1905 Revolution
note: 9 January in the Old Style calendar.

name: Moroccan crises
summary: Tangier (1905) and Agadir (1911).

name: Austria-Hungary declares war on Serbia
aliases: outbreak of the First World War

name: February Revolution in Russia
note: 23-27 February in the Old Style calendar.

name: United States enters the First World War
aliases: US entry into the First World War

name: October Revolution (Bolshevik seizure of power)
note: 25 October in the Old Style calendar.

name: Armistice ends the First World War
League of Nations comes into being
Munich Agreement
note: Signed in the early hours of 30 September; dated 29 September.

name: Britain and France declare war on Germany
aliases: outbreak of the Second World War

name: Battle of Stalingrad
summary: German surrender on 2 February 1943.

name: UN Charter signed at San Francisco
Indonesian independence proclaimed
summary: Dutch recognition followed on 27 December 1949.

name: Japan signs the instrument of surrender
National Party victory; apartheid policy begins
Treaty of Paris creates the ECSC
Geneva Accords on Indochina
summary: Vietnam divided at the 17th parallel.

name: Nasser nationalises the Suez Canal Company
Treaty of Rome (EEC)
summary: EEC in operation from 1 January 1958.

name: Great Leap Forward
note: Some works date its end to 1961-62.

name: Year of Africa
summary: Seventeen African states become independent.

name: Dissolution of the Soviet Union
aliases: dissolution of the USSR|collapse of the Soviet Union

name: Maastricht Treaty signed
summary: In force from 1 November 1993.

name: Euro introduced
summary: Notes and coins from 1 January 2002.
